sources.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (2017 v2)
sources.locator: Contents pp. 5–6; ch. 8 pp. 47–52 complete; Theorem 6.4 and Remark 6.5 p. 37; ch. 9 Norm Estimates and Examples 9.3–9.4 pp. 54–55 only

contents.name: Chapter 8: Fourier series: convergence at a point
contents.support: Full chapter read; local positive criteria retained at their published homes; deep theorem recorded, not proved.

contents.name: Theorem 8.1 (Kolmogorov)
contents.support: Source states unbounded divergence everywhere. Batch deliberately uses only the weaker a.e. assertion, independently verified with a complete construction in G.

contents.name: Theorem 8.2
contents.support: Full functional-analytic proof read. The norm equality extracted into lem-fourier-partial-sum-operator-norm-equals-the-lebesgue-constant.

contents.name: Another proof [Katznelson Sec II.2]
contents.reason: The chapter refers out to an explicit dense-set construction. FR-5 chooses Banach–Steinhaus and a prescribed point; this pointer is not treated as a read proof of the other construction.

contents.name: Exercise: uniform convergence for Holder continuous f
contents.reason: This strengthens the local positive regularity branch, not the divergence/maximal endpoint branch commissioned in FR-5. It is not needed by any local proof here.

contents.name: Corollary 8.5 (Localization Principle)
contents.support: Context only: if f vanishes near x then S_N f(x)->0 by the published Dini criterion; hence the divergent witness cannot vanish near its bad point. Include this short implication in the witness discussion, without a second theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 8.7 (Carleson–Hunt)
contents.support: Both the a.e. statement and strong maximal estimate in the omitted-proof paragraph are read. Closure carried by cor-lp-fourier-series-converges-almost-everywhere-for-p-greater-than-one.

contents.name: Theorem 6.4 (Maximal functions and convergence a.e.)
contents.locator: p. 37, full theorem and proof for finite q
contents.support: Specialize to p=q finite and Fourier sums; use explicit Fejer polynomial approximation.

contents.name: Remark 6.5
contents.support: The weak quantitative estimate gives qualitative closure; batch writes the level-set proof.

contents.name: Norm Estimates
contents.support: C(T) upper norm estimate; no use of an upper bound to prove divergence.

contents.name: Example 9.3 (Divergence in C(T))
contents.support: The operator norm equals the Lebesgue constant; also gives uniform-norm unboundedness for the pointwise witness.

contents.name: Example 9.4 (Divergence in L1(T))
contents.support: Read Fejer-test proof of the L1 operator norm lower bound and its Banach–Steinhaus consequence. Include the consequence as a contextual application under DC; no new theorem label.

contents.name: Aside: explicit L1 norm divergence, Grafakos Exercise 3.5.9
contents.reason: The cited exercise is an alternative explicit construction, not read here. The locally supplied Fejer tests already refute strong (1,1), and the A page retains Kolmogorov separately.

sources.title: Loukas Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, 3rd ed.
sources.locator: Contents p. xiv; §3.4.3 pp. 210–211 complete; §4.2.1 pp. 255–261 complete; §4.2.2 opening/Theorem 4.2.5 statement p. 261 only

contents.name: 3.4.3 Pointwise Divergence of the Dirichlet Means
Proposition 3.4.6(a) (duBois Reymond)
contents.support: Real continuous sign-approximation tests and uniform boundedness; full proof read.

contents.name: Proposition 3.4.6(b)
contents.reason: This is the n-dimensional square-sum extension F(x)=f(x1) diverging on a hyperplane. The assigned pair is the one-dimensional torus; no local proof needs multiple Fourier series.

contents.name: 4.2 A. E. Divergence of Fourier Series and Bochner–Riesz means
contents.support: Only Fourier-series subsection is used as backing; boundary to spherical means is explicitly recorded below.

contents.name: 4.2.1 Divergence of Fourier Series of Integrable Functions
Theorem 4.2.1
contents.support: Conclusion is unbounded a.e. divergence, proved at (4.2.13), not convergence failure merely in norm.

contents.name: Lemma 4.2.2 (Kronecker)
contents.support: Record as an unsupplied construction cost: if 1,x1,...,xN are Q-linearly independent, any prescribed unimodular phases are simultaneously approximated by exp(2*pi*i*L*xj) for some integer L. Full Fourier averaging proof read; no local logical use.

contents.name: Lemma 4.2.3
contents.support: Unsupplied construction cost: probability measures mu_N with sup_L|D_L*mu_N|>=c log N a.e.; full atomic measure and phase-alignment proof read.

contents.name: Lemma 4.2.4
contents.support: Exact integer M>=1 specialization: nonnegative unit-L1 polynomial, maximal height >2^M, good set measure >1-2^-M. Read finite-maximal truncation and Fejer smoothing.

contents.name: Weighted polynomial series (4.2.7)–(4.2.13)
contents.support: Read recursive epsilon and M choices, degree controls, early/tail estimates, and full-measure limsup conclusion. Source architecture is not a local proof.

contents.name: 4.2.2 Divergence of Bochner–Riesz Means of Integrable Functions
contents.locator: p. 261 heading and opening statement only
contents.reason: This separate spherical-summability branch is excluded in the design coverage ledger. No proof from pp. 262–270 is claimed read or used; the exact complete Fourier range is pp. 255–261.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2.5
contents.reason: Critical-index spherical means on T^n for n>1, including localized support, are distinct from the symmetric one-dimensional sums on this pair. Its proof is not part of the harvested range.

sources.title: Michael T. Lacey, Carleson’s Theorem: Proof, Complements, Variations (arXiv v4)
sources.locator: Contents pp. 1–2; §1 pp. 2–4; §3 pp. 11–14 before §3.1; §7 opening and §7.1 pp. 24–26; §7.2 opening p. 26 through (7.9) only

contents.name: 1. Introduction
contents.support: Read oscillatory obstruction and three-stage architecture; the real-line normalization is not substituted for the torus definition.

contents.name: Proposition 1.4
contents.support: Independent treatment of limsup error <= maximal approximation error plus pointwise approximation error, under an explicit weak bound.

contents.name: Carleson’s Theorem
contents.support: Real-line L2 theorem and Hunt extension named; torus backing is Laugesen. No local transference claim.

contents.name: 3. The Central Lemmas
contents.support: Read tile order, trees, count, density, size and summation of scales; not a proof of the three input lemmas.

contents.name: Lemma 3.6 (Density Lemma)
contents.support: Halve the residual density while controlling sum of tree-top lengths by inverse density.

contents.name: Lemma 3.9 (Size Lemma)
contents.support: Halve residual size with inverse-square size control of tree-top lengths.

contents.name: Lemma 3.11 (Tree Lemma)
contents.support: Tree contribution controlled by top length times size times density.

contents.name: Final summation (3.13)–(3.16)
contents.support: Balance density with squared size and sum min(2^-n,2^n).

contents.name: 7. Carleson’s Theorem on Lp, 1<p!=2<infinity
contents.support: Read distributional estimate and interpolation route; no claim that full proof §7 was read.

contents.name: Proposition 7.1
contents.support: Restricted distributional estimate for the model operator; retained only in proof-cost discussion.

contents.name: 7.1 The case of |F|<1/3
contents.support: Rebalances counts and sums scale contributions to |F| |log |F||.

contents.name: 7.2 The case of |F|>=3
contents.support: Read exceptional set Omega={M 1_E>C1/|F|}, choose F prime outside it and split tiles. Remaining proof is not claimed read.
